title: Mesoporous g-C3N4 nanosheets with improved photocatalytic performance for hydrogen evolution

lanes.label: Classical tools
lanes.sub: collapsed to one node per state

states.title: Hypothesis and design
states.head: Bulk g-C3N4 is a thick multilayer stack with low surface area, which limits its photocatalytic H2 evolution. Exfoliating bulk g-C3N4 into thin mesoporous nanosheets should raise photocatalytic hydrogen evolution.
states.detail: Absorbed: n1 (HYP/need), n2 (HYP/hypothesis), n3 (DES/base_system), n4 (DES/route), n5 (PRC/treatment)

states.title: Structure state
states.head: Exfoliation turns micron-sized stacked BCN blocks into few-layer 2D nanosheets. CNS has a much larger specific surface area (7.61 -> 55.41 m2/g) and mesopore volume (0.055 -> 0.216 cm3/g).
states.detail: Absorbed: n6 (STR/microstructure/shape), n7 (STR/microstructure/porosity), n18 (STR/microstructure/porosity). Premises: Type IV isotherm with H3 hysteresis indicates mesopores (slit-shaped, from plate aggregates)

states.title: Property state and mechanisms
states.head: CNS has a narrower optical bandgap than BCN (2.51 vs 2.68 eV). CNS absorbs more light than BCN over 250-800 nm.
states.detail: Absorbed: n9 (PRP/value), n10 (PRP/value), n11 (PRP/descriptor), n12 (MEC/pathway). Premises: Lower steady-state PL intensity means less radiative electron-hole recombination, i.e. better separation; A smaller Nyquist arc radius means lower charge-transfer resistance; Exfoliated g-C3N4 nanosheets in earlier work show more active sites and shorter carrier migration paths than bulk

states.title: Performance state
states.head: Photocatalytic H2 evolution rate of CNS is 3.3 times that of BCN (97.6 vs 29.8 umol g-1 h-1)

states.title: Conclusion
states.head: Ultrasonic exfoliation gives mesoporous g-C3N4 nanosheets that keep the g-C3N4 structure and evolve H2 about 3.3 times faster than bulk g-C3N4
